what.text: NAD+ (nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide) is a coenzyme found in every living cell. Enzymes use it to move electrons in energy metabolism, and other enzymes use it up as a raw material. The body makes it from forms of vitamin B3, such as nicotinamide and nicotinamide riboside.

src.label: Grant et al., Front Aging Neurosci, 2019

what.text: When NAD+ was infused into a vein in a small 2019 study, it was cleared from the blood quickly for the first 2 hours. The breakdown products found fit with enzymes breaking NAD+ down.

src.label: Grant et al., Front Aging Neurosci, 2019

what.text: No study has shown that injected or nasal NAD+ slows aging in people.

research.text: Human evidence for injected NAD+ is small. We found one pilot study of an IV infusion in 11 healthy men, one chart review of 14 clinic clients, and two randomized trials in China that used a hospital NAD+ injection for heart disease, not for aging. We found no published human study of NAD+ nasal spray.
Each is listed below as it was run.

research.title: IV infusion in healthy men, 2019

facts.v: Pilot study. Participants were randomized to NAD+ or saline. Run at a wellness clinic in Springfield, Louisiana.
11 healthy men aged 30 to 55: 8 got NAD+, 3 got saline
One 6-hour IV infusion, with blood and urine sampled up to 8 hours
NAD+ and its breakdown products in blood and urine; liver blood tests; side effects

research.found: Blood NAD+ did not rise for the first 2 hours. Breakdown products and some NAD+ appeared in urine by 6 hours. No adverse events were seen in either group. Some liver enzyme readings fell slightly at 8 hours.

src.label: Grant et al., Front Aging Neurosci, 2019

research.title: IV NAD+ vs IV nicotinamide riboside, 2026

facts.v: Look-back review of medical records at a commercial wellness business in Austin, Texas. No placebo. The authors worked for the business.
14 adult clients: 6 got IV NAD+, 8 got IV nicotinamide riboside
Four infusions on four days in a row, then 30 days of follow-up
Symptoms during infusion, infusion time, blood pressure, heart rate, liver, kidney, thyroid and inflammation blood tests

research.found: People getting NAD+ reported moderate to severe stomach and gut symptoms, faster heart rate and chest pressure during infusions, which slowed the infusions. Symptoms stopped when the infusion ended. Most blood tests did not change. HDL cholesterol fell in the NAD+ group.

src.label: Reyna et al., Front Aging, 2026

research.title: Heart failure after heart muscle damage, 2025 (China)

facts.v: Single-center, randomized, placebo-controlled trial, on top of standard heart-failure care
180 adults with heart failure from ischemic cardiomyopathy
IV NAD+ or placebo daily for 7 days; follow-up to 6 months
Change in heart pumping (LVEF) at 1 month; NT-proBNP; heart and stroke events; symptom class

research.found: LVEF at 1 month was higher in the NAD+ group than with placebo (45.4% vs 42.4%). Differences in NT-proBNP, heart events and symptom class were not statistically significant. This was a heart-disease trial, not an aging trial.

src.label: Yu et al., Am J Cardiovasc Drugs, 2026 (heart failure)

research.title: After a heart attack and stenting, 2026 (China)

facts.v: Randomized, placebo-controlled trial, same hospital group as above
120 patients treated for ST-elevation heart attack with emergency stenting
IV NAD+ or placebo daily for 7 days; follow-up to 6 months
LVEF at 30 days; NT-proBNP; heart and stroke events at 6 months

research.found: LVEF at 30 days was modestly higher with NAD+ (56.3% vs 53.4%). NT-proBNP was lower. Heart and stroke events at 6 months did not differ.

src.label: Yu et al., Am J Cardiovasc Drugs, 2026 (heart attack)

research.text: Registered trials with no results yet

research.title: Children with weak heart pumping (PEDI-NAD)

facts.v: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled; sponsored by Beijing Children's Hospital
180 children planned, in hospital with LVEF below 55%
IV once daily for 7 days; follow-up to 48 weeks
Change in LVEF at 4 weeks

research.found: Not yet recruiting as of its September 2026 posting. The record says the injection used is a marketed product in China.

src.label: NCT07839130 (PEDI-NAD), ClinicalTrials.gov

research.text: We found no published human study of NAD+ given as a nasal spray. One 2026 study gave NAD+ into the nose of mice with a chemically damaged sense of smell, and tested NAD+ on human smell stem cells in a dish. This is animal and cell evidence only.

src.label: Yoo et al., Exp Mol Med, 2026

research.text: Most research on NAD+ biology is in cells and animals. The authors of the 2019 pilot wrote that, before their study, no data were available on what happens to directly infused NAD+ in people. Animal results have not been shown to apply to injected or nasal NAD+ in people.

us.text: NAD+ is not FDA approved for any use. It sits in FDA's 503A Category 1, the group of nominated substances still under evaluation, which pharmacies may compound under FDA's interim policy if its conditions are met. That is not approval. As of October 31, 2026.

items.text: none. A search of FDA's Drugs@FDA data found no product with NAD as an active ingredient.

world.lead: No regulator we checked has approved NAD+ as a medicine for aging. Health Canada lists NAD+ among unauthorized injectables it has seized. A Chinese trial record says an NAD+ injection is marketed in China; we could not confirm that with China's regulator. NAD+ is not named on the WADA list.

after.text: NAD+ is not named on the 2026 WADA Prohibited List or on the 2027 list. Separately, the list prohibits intravenous infusions or injections of more than 100 mL in total per 12-hour period at all times (method M2.2), except those legitimately received in hospital treatment, surgery or clinical diagnostic investigations. That rule is about the method, whatever the substance. The 2027 list, which takes effect January 1, 2027, keeps the same rule.

side.text: The human studies were small and short. Side effects reported during IV NAD+ include stomach and gut symptoms, a faster heart rate and chest pressure. FDA has also received reports of severe chills, shaking and vomiting after NAD+ injections, consistent with endotoxin contamination.

items.text: in the 2026 chart review, people given IV NAD+ reported moderate to severe gut symptoms, faster heart rate and chest pressure. These stopped when the infusion ended. The 2019 pilot reported no adverse events in 8 men.

unconfirmed: We could not confirm NAD+'s status with the MHRA (UK), the EMA or EU national regulators.
We could not reach the TGA's product register (ARTG) to check for any NAD+ product in Australia.
We could not confirm with China's NMPA that an NAD+ (Coenzyme I) injection is approved there; only a trial record says so.
We found no published human study of NAD+ nasal spray, so its safety and effects in people are unknown.
We found no WADA statement on whether S0 (non-approved substances) could apply to NAD+ products; NAD+ is simply not named.
surprises: NAD+ is widely sold as an anti-aging injection, but we found no human trial of injected or nasal NAD+ that measured aging; the largest human studies used it for heart disease in China.
Health Canada lists NAD+ among the unauthorized injectable 'peptide' drugs it has seized, although NAD+ is a coenzyme, not a peptide.
In the 2019 IV pilot, blood NAD+ did not rise at all for the first 2 hours of infusion, which cuts against the idea that an infusion simply tops up NAD+ in the blood.
